en: Now let's build our first basic tree data
structure, and let's start with a concrete
example. We're building an application that

because you're building a Dropbox-like

allow users to manage folders and files,

system, and if we take a closer look at that

got multiple folders
and in those folders we could have files.
So both a folder and a file is basically
just a node, a vertex in that tree.
And then the connections that describe the
file system are our edges.
So in the end, a file system is a tree and
this shows you why tree data structures
matter. It's very easy to imagine
applications that need to deal with file
systems internally in code, for example, a
Dropbox-like application.
Now I can also say right away that we will
not just use trees for file systems. Of
course,
there are also other kinds of data which we

helpful, but a file system should be an

So how could we now
build a data structure that allows us to add
new folders or files,
and there isn't a big difference in the end
here, by the way, in the tree, whether it's
a folder or a file, it's simply a node.
So how do we build such a data structure
that allows us to add nodes and connect
those nodes?
Well, if we think about it carefully,
the tree as a whole
isn't really
that special. It's just a combination of all
the nodes, right? In the end, the node is
the interesting data structure here.
We have a node that is connected to another
node or to multiple other nodes potentially.
A node can have multiple children after all.
And then those nodes also can have more
children.
And the tree is really just the combination
of all those nodes and the only thing that
matters to the tree is what the root node
is.
So the tree data structure is fairly simple.
It could be as simple as an object that
simply keeps track of the root node.
And then every node itself could also be an
object which has a children array, which is
a list of all the nested, the child nodes,
and maybe a pointer at the parent node it
belongs to so that we have a pointer in both
directions to the children and to the
parent.
Well, let's start with that and let's
implement such a basic tree.
